status.title: Google Quantum AI: Verifiable Quantum Circuit Compilation
status.headline: We are building the cheapest quantum circuits we can for three tasks, and our best graded entry so far scored 24.77234 on 5 November. We are now checking public ideas for further savings and have not sent a newer entry since.

board.note: Score is Kaggle's graded result for our 5 November entry. No board place has been read since 24 October, when we were 56th of 723 teams at a score of 8.87, so the current place is not known.

entries.note: Counts read from Kaggle just before our 5 November entry (2 used that day, 41 in all, 3 still allowed) plus that one entry. Nothing newer is recorded.

next: Keep reading the public discussions and notebooks for cheaper circuit ideas.
Test any promising idea against the contest's own checking programs before sending it.
Close the open safety checks on our best entry before choosing the two final entries.

status.title: Predicting Credit Card Fraud
status.headline: We are in the top few hundred of about a thousand teams on the public board and our best entry scores about as well as the leaders. We are widening the set of models we blend and have until the end of November to send final entries.

board.note: The place was read on 7 November before our later entries; the best score is from our ninth entry the same day, so today's place is likely better than the one shown.

entries.note: Count is the entries logged in the ledger on main as of 7 November; entries used today are not recorded there. The daily limit of ten is from the contest rules page read on 1 November.

next: Run the full-recipe language-model member on one fold of rented cards to see if it adds to the blend.
Keep scouting public notebooks and prediction banks and blend in any that check out on our own validation split.
